subject: Billing true-up and seat-vs-token rounding FAQ for BrightCart
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Moreno <lisa@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Billing true-up and seat-vs-token rounding FAQ for BrightCart

Hi Lisa / BrightCart procurement team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached are two simple scenario workbooks that show how the proposed combination of 50 committed seats + a burst token buffer would behave across a few usage profiles. Before we lock the SOW language we wanted to confirm a few billing mechanics so there are no surprises on month 1 and at true-up: 

Key items we want to make explicit and confirm with you:
- What the committed seat covers: seats include dedicated concurrency and a per-seat monthly credit equivalent to 200k generation tokens (these credits stack across seats).
- Burst buffer: any consumption above committed credits is billed at the overage per-token rate with a soft-burst allowance in a given day to avoid transient spikes triggering immediate large invoices.
- Long-context sessions: sessions that exceed 16k context are billed on the total token footprint for the call; we round billing to the nearest 100-token increment for generation requests, and to the nearest 50-token increment for embeddings.
- True-up cadence: our standard is quarterly true-up with invoice adjustment; we can do monthly true-up on request for enterprise accounting workflows (will show as additional line items).

Action items for you: can you send 1-2 representative weekly peaks (session lengths and approximate number of concurrent users) so we can pick the right commit level? With those numbers we’ll populate the workbook and show estimated monthly invoices under both the seat-first and token-commit options.

I’ve attached: RC_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx (3 tabs: baseline, spike, long-session) and a one-pager Seat_vs_Token_Math.pdf.

If helpful I can do a short 30-min call where we walk the math with your finance and engineering folks — propose Monday 11/16 10a PT.

Thanks,
Markus Klein

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing true-up and seat-vs-token rounding FAQ for BrightCart

Thanks Markus — quick follow-ups: 

Appreciate the workbook. Two clarifications before we review with finance: 
1) For one of our use cases we have intermittent 30–40k token long threads (customer support transcripts) but 95% of sessions are under 3k tokens. If we hit a 40k spike, does the rounding (to 100 tokens) meaningfully change the bill? Example: if that call generates 40,175 tokens, are we charged for 40,200? Or is there per-call minimums we should be aware of?

2) True-up cadence: our procurement team prefers monthly reconciliation to avoid large quarterly catches. Would monthly true-up incur any premium?

We’re also interested in an option where commits include a small long-context reserve to avoid overage for a small number of long transcripts per month — curious if that’s something you already price as an add-on.

Can we do the Monday slot you proposed — Jordan (CC’d) will join from our engineering team.

—Lisa
Director, Product Operations
BrightCart

On a practical note: procurement@brightcart.com -> who I loop here for contract language/POs.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: BrightCart billing clarifications — internal proposal

Markus / Jordan —

Quick draft response and negotiation posture for the call. Summarized points we can share publicly vs internal negotiation levers: 

Public (share on call):
- Rounding & per-call math: generation tokens are rounded up to the nearest 100-token increment. So a 40,175-token call will bill as 40,200 generation tokens. Embedding calls round to 50-token increments. No additional per-call minimum beyond those increments.
- Long-context reserve: we can include a pooled long-context reserve (example: 1M long-context tokens/month) priced at a fixed add-on and consumed before overage applies. This prevents an infrequent 40k spike from immediately incurring overage charges.
- True-up cadence: we offer monthly reconciliation as an enterprise option (no rate premium) provided they accept electronic invoicing and PO terms in our standard template. Quarterly true-up is default for commercial deals.

Internal (negotiation levers):
- If they want the pooled reserve included in committed seats, ask for +10% commit increase or a 6-month minimum on the reserve add-on.
- For monthly true-up without prepayment, require a 30-day settlement SLA and add a "rolling offset" clause that reduces committed credits if invoices are late more than 45 days.

Example math (from workbook tab):
- Option A (Seat-first): 50 seats x 200k token credit = 10M tokens/month included. Residual = billed at $0.0008/token (burst rate).
- Option B (Token commit): 8M committed tokens @ $0.00065/token with 10% burst buffer priced at $0.00085/token for overage.
- Spike scenario: single 40k call rounded to 40,200 tokens -> cost at burst $0.00085 = $34.17 for that call if it sits on overage; if within pooled reserve = $0.

I attached a version of the workbook with both options modeled and our recommended starting position (Seat-first + 1M reserve).

Neha
Head of Commercial Pricing (internal)
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Internal note: if procurement pushes monthly true-up without PO + prepayment, escalate to finance for risk signoff.

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing true-up and seat-vs-token rounding FAQ for BrightCart

Hi Lisa — thanks for the questions, answered inline and with a short FAQ below. Jordan — great that you can join Monday, we’ll walk the workbook together.

1) Rounding and examples
- Rounding policy: generation calls bill to the next 100-token increment. So 40,175 -> 40,200 (billed tokens). That increases that single-call charge by the incremental 25 tokens in this case; at our overage rate that translates to a small delta (see math below).
- No further per-call minimum beyond the rounding increment.

2) Long-context spikes and pooled reserve
- We offer a pooled long-context reserve add-on that is consumed before overage. If you expect ~5 long transcripts per week (30–40k each) the reserve prevents repeated overage charges. Our recommended starting reserve is 1M long-context tokens/month for your profile.

3) True-up cadence and pricing
- Monthly true-up: available at no additional per-token premium, requires electronic invoicing and standard PO terms (examples included in the workbook). Quarterly default otherwise.

Quick cost example (from attached workbook):
- Overaged call cost (rounded to 100): 40,200 tokens x $0.00085 = $34.17.
- If inside pooled reserve: $0 for that call (reserve consumed instead).

Next steps:
- Jordan / procurement: please paste two real usage samples (one baseline week and one peak week) into tab 'input' of the workbook and we’ll update the SOW language to include the long-context reserve clause.
- Call: Monday 11/16 10:00a PT — invite sent.

Thanks — look forward to closing this out quickly.

Markus Klein
Account Executive — Platform Sales
Redwood Inference
